## TL;DR

This hygiene pass found nothing `repoos gc` is willing to remove. At 2026-11-04T23:10Z, `repoos status --json` counted 22 Git worktrees, 19 of them managed by RepoOS. `repoos gc --dry-run` listed 0 safe candidates, 18 retained task worktrees, and 3 worktrees that live outside RepoOS's managed directory. `repoos gc --yes` was not run. No worktree or branch was deleted by hand. Before and after counts are identical. The previous handoff died at the commit step because the branch has no product diff; this run records `no_source_change: true` so a no-op handoff is allowed, and it records every retained reason in the task's Cleanup report.

## Work and rationale

The task is a scheduled pass, not a code change. The runbook is explicit: review registered worktrees, remove only what RepoOS itself proves safe with `repoos gc`, and otherwise leave the tree alone. Safe means the command's own candidate list. A done or archived task with a leftover worktree is not automatically safe. Several retained entries are done tasks whose worktrees still fail a content check ("task file content not represented in main") or still have dirty task files. The notes point those at the safety rules tracked in #1004. Judging them removable from the path or the `done` status would be the failure mode this task exists to avoid.

I started from the live board rather than from memory of earlier sessions. `repoos driver brief` and `repoos list` showed this task active alongside other live work, including the easter-eggs bundle #1026. `repoos status --json` then gave the worktree inventory from the main checkout that owns the worktrees (the CLI warns when it is invoked inside a linked worktree and reports that checkout). The managed count was 19, the warn threshold is 20, and `candidates` was an empty array. `counts` were candidates 0, retained 18, external 3. The board slice of that status also showed active tasks #1008, #1009, and #1026, plus review task #1025 still marked "task agent still active" by gc. `repoos list` a couple of minutes later printed #1008 and #1026 as the active column. I did not treat that flicker as permission to collect #1009. Its gc reason was "task agent still active" and its worktree was dirty (`src/ui-app/tests/remote-validation.test.ts`). Dirty plus an active agent is protected even if a later list view drops the row.

`repoos gc --dry-run` repeated the same split in prose: "0 safe candidates · 18 retained · 3 outside RepoOS". Each retained line carries the exact reason I copied into the task. The classes were:

- An agent is still active (#1026, #1025, #1009, and this task #1008).
- The task is human-assigned and close-out does not resolve it (#0794, `feat/live-verification-of-jev-and-clef-flash-`). `repoos list` still shows #0794 in ready, which matches "do not collect a human-owned task."
- Uncommitted task-file changes that gc calls unique data (work/0534, work/0591, work/0595, work/0589, work/0592, work/0599, and the dirty task file on the hold task #0960).
- Ignored paths that may hold local data on #0960 (`src/ui-app/.repoos/auto-engineering-decision.json`, `work/.attachments`).
- Task-file content not represented in main, or source changes not in main, on several done branches including #0898, #0830, #0834, #0840, the check-cache branch, the shot-capture branch, and `feat/upload-state-retry-ux` (9 commits ahead and a large dirty tree).

The three external worktrees are Codex checkouts under `~/.codex/worktrees/`. The task says those are not this pass's to remove. I left them.

Because the candidate list was empty, the acceptance rule forbids `repoos gc --yes`. I did not run it. I also did not run `git worktree remove` or `git branch -D`. A second cleanup was unnecessary: nothing in this session touches a worktree registration, so the after count is the before count (22 total, 19 managed, 0 candidates, 18 retained, 3 external). The driver brief still lists older close-outs failing with "feature branch worktree not found" (#0195, #0278, #0267). Those are missing worktrees, not leftovers gc can collect. Creating or repairing them is outside this task.

No product file was edited. The only task-file edits are this task's own frontmatter flag and the Cleanup report. Nothing was pushed. No other task was started.

## Approaches tried

The first attempt in the previous session ended without a handoff. The queued failure is specific: "handoff failed at step commit: no implementation found since the branch diverged; use no_source_change: true to force a no-op handoff." That matches the review guard. It treats the task's own markdown as bookkeeping, so a report-only diff is still "no implementation" unless `no_source_change` is set. I set `no_source_change: true` on this worktree's task file. There is no `repoos update` flag for that field; the guard's own error text is the instruction to set it for a legitimate no-op.

I also ran `repoos update 1008 --section "Cleanup report"`. From inside the linked worktree the CLI writes the main checkout's board copy and says so. The worktree copy is what this branch will commit, so the same report is in the worktree task file as well. Acceptance checkboxes in that worktree copy are marked done for this pass. The empty-candidate branch of the second checkbox is satisfied by not running `repoos gc --yes`.

I considered whether any retained done worktree was "obviously merged" and should be forced. The dry-run already refused them, and the runbook says to leave unresolved done or archived worktrees for #1004. I did not override that.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree count sits one under the warn threshold (19 managed, threshold 20) while still holding 18 trees gc will not touch. The noise the task describes is real, and this pass cannot clear it without weakening the guard. That is a product limit, not a failed run. The close-out errors about missing feature-branch worktrees are the opposite problem (worktrees already gone) and were not "fixed" by deleting more trees.

`repoos status` and `repoos list` disagreed slightly on whether #1009 was still in the active column. gc's retained reason was the stricter signal, and the worktree was dirty, so it stayed.

The handoff path will not accept a branch that only updates this task file unless the no-source-change flag is present. Setting that flag is the whole fix for the restarted session. Scoped `repoos check` still has to pass before the handoff request.

## Key learnings

`repoos gc` is the only removal authority on this schedule. An empty candidate list is a successful run: the report is the deliverable, and the worktree inventory is unchanged. Reasons are per worktree and must be copied from the dry-run, not inferred from `status: done`. External worktrees and anything with an active agent, a human assignee, a dirty tree, or task-file content gc cannot see in main stay put. A hygiene task with no product diff has to opt into `no_source_change` or the commit step of handoff rejects it the same way the previous session was rejected.
